import sys, json, datetime

# The fan-in of the builder's tool loop. A shrunk `collector/assemble`: the four
# algorithms that carry, none of the eleven lanes that do not.
#
# Every knob is read from `params`, which the substrate always sets -- so two
# builders in one colony are tuned apart, and a mutation retunes one without
# touching a colony-wide environment.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
env = doc["envelope"]
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _int(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    if v is None:
        return default
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


# The loop begins at the seam, so the seam ends it. At the cap the collected
# thread leaves for `normalise` instead of asking the composer again.
MAX_ITER = _int("max_iter", 6)
# GH #485 -- the WRITING budget, and it is a different budget from the round
# budget for the same reason the repair budget is: a model that spends every
# round it has on looking has none left for the answer, and looking is what a
# model does when nothing stops it. Measured against a hosted Sonnet-class
# model: seven rounds, thirteen tool calls, not one text turn, and a build that
# ended paid-for and empty.
#
# So the last `write_rounds` rounds of a build are WRITING rounds and the tool
# menu is withheld from them. That is a mechanism and not a sentence in a
# prompt: with no `tools` in the system tree the request carries no tool array,
# so a tool call is not a move the wire admits and answering is the only one
# left. The briefing announces it from round 0 (`brief`, BUDGET), because a
# budget a model learns about in its last round is one it could not plan
# against.
WRITE_ROUNDS = _int("write_rounds", 1)
# A SEPARATE budget, and that is the whole point: a model that burns its round
# budget on searches would have none left for the refusal it could actually
# repair.
MAX_REPAIRS = _int("max_repairs", 2)
# A round whose result never arrives must not park until the TTL: a TTL death is
# SILENT (direct to DLQ, no reply_to cascade), so the tool_call_id waiting at
# `templates/tools/build-draft` would never be closed.
ROUND_IDLE_MS = _int("round_idle_ms", 120000)

FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)
# Fixed-width UTC timestamps order lexicographically, so this is a string
# compare. Pure arithmetic, no timer of the template's own.
IDLE_CUT = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
            - datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=ROUND_IDLE_MS)).strftime(FMT)

hop = (env.get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {}
ctx = (env.get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
build_id = str(ctx.get("build_id") or hop.get("build_id") or "")
it = int(ctx.get("iter", 0) or 0)
repairs = int(ctx.get("repairs", 0) or 0)
msgs = d.get("messages") or []

# GH #460 -- the caller's coordinates, and why the loop writes them down.
#
# A `/colony` eye's reply starts a FRESH trace, so the edge `./eyes -> ./weave`
# restores exactly the three coordinates the LOOP needs. Everything the CALLER
# needs was on no list, and which of the two travels on is decided by a RACE:
# the slate of a round is read by the leg that arrives LAST, and it is that
# leg's context that goes forward. A `lib` leg carries the caller, an eye does
# not -- so a round an eye won handed the requester a draft under an EMPTY
# tool_call_id, and the tool round that asked for it never closed.
#
# So the caller is written down, in the one place that survives a foreign chain:
# this loop's own round table -- the same shape `normalise` uses for the digest
# binding. The row is parked when the composer OPENS a round (the one leg that
# is always on the build's own chain) and read back whenever a round is decided.
#
# GH #480 -- the DOOR is one of these coordinates, and it was not on the list.
# `meclaw-os` stamps `build_caller` (and `build_auto_submit`) once, at its rim,
# and the four edges out of `./builder` read them back to decide between the
# operator's front door and `./orgs`. They were lost to exactly the two breaks
# above: an eye's reply, and a receipt arriving on the submitter's chain. An
# operator-initiated build that consulted the graph and then SUCCEEDED delivered
# its manifest into an organisation -- and in a fresh colony `./orgs` is empty by
# construction, so that is a silent dead letter. The two keys travel with the
# other four because they are lost by the same mechanism and recovered by it.
CALLER_KEYS = ("build_call_id", "agent", "build_op", "build_scope",
               "build_caller", "build_auto_submit")
caller = {k: str(ctx.get(k) or "") for k in CALLER_KEYS}


def names_a_caller(said):
    """Whether a caller map says anything at all.

    `build_call_id` alone used to be the test, and an OPERATOR-driven build has
    none -- there is no agent tool call behind a person at the front door. So
    the one build whose door could not be recovered any other way was the one
    build that never wrote its row (GH #480)."""
    return any(str(said.get(k) or "") for k in CALLER_KEYS)
# `orig_request` rides in the ROW and never in the hop: it is prose, and a
# header is not where prose belongs. Nothing downstream reads it back out of the
# context either -- `builder-librarian/retrieve` re-sets it from `hop.orig` on
# every lookup of its own -- so the row is the record and the hop stays short.


def park():
    """Terminal by design: an incomplete fan-in and a lost race emit NOTHING."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(out):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))
    sys.exit(0)


def head(route, extra=None):
    """Every emission carries the full key set the edges read. A missing hop key
    makes a CEL modifier fail, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge -- so keys
    are present and empty rather than absent."""
    out = {"route": route, "build_id": build_id, "iter": str(it),
           "repairs": str(repairs)}
    out.update(caller)
    if extra:
        out.update(extra)
    return out


def store_bundle(ops):
    """Insert and read-back in ONE message (GH #419). The store runs a bundle's
    ops in order over its one connection, so the trailing select sees the insert
    in front of it: of N legs parking concurrently exactly ONE reads a complete
    set. No guard row to win, no message to win it with."""
    return {"header": head("cstore"),
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                          "id": name, "text": json.dumps(op)}
                         for name, op in ops]}


def park_and_read(role, turn, fired=0, iter_=None, before=()):
    """`before` rides in FRONT of the round row and inside the SAME bundle: the
    store runs a bundle's ops in order over its one connection, so the trailing
    select sees every insert ahead of it and the ordering guarantee that carries
    the round carries these too."""
    return store_bundle(list(before) + [
        ("w-round-row",
         {"operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
          "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": it if iter_ is None else iter_,
                  "role": role, "turn": json.dumps(turn), "fired": fired,
                  "recorded_at": now}}),
        ("w-round-read",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "thread",
          "columns": ["build_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired", "recorded_at"],
          "where": {"build_id": build_id}})])


# The private format of a receipt turn: the code NAMED at the front. Written
# here and read here, which is what lets the give_up header recover it without a
# column the transcript does not have.
REFUSED = "the submission was refused: "


def code_of(r):
    """The error_code a receipt row was written with, back out of its turn."""
    try:
        t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
    except Exception:
        return ""
    text = str((t or {}).get("text") or "") if isinstance(t, dict) else ""
    if not text.startswith(REFUSED):
        return ""
    return text[len(REFUSED):].split(" -- ", 1)[0].strip()


def has_slot(body, slot):
    """Whether a leg answered at all -- an empty result and an absent one are
    different facts, and only one of them ends a build."""
    return any(m.get("id") == slot for m in (body.get("messages") or []))


def rows_of(body, slot):
    """The slate one leg of a bundle came back with. The store answers a bundle
    with one `tool_result` turn per leg in `messages[]`, keyed by that leg's
    `tool_call_id`; the top-level `results[]` slot carries per-op METADATA only
    (`store/output.rs`, `build_bundle_result`), so the rows are read here."""
    for m in (body.get("messages") or []):
        if m.get("id") == slot and m.get("text"):
            try:
                r = json.loads(m["text"])
            except Exception:
                return []
            return r if isinstance(r, list) else []
    return []


def round_sets(rows, iter_):
    """The fan-in state of ONE iteration, read from the slate: the call ids the
    assistant expects, the ids that answered, and the newest write time of the
    round -- its last PROGRESS. A row that cannot be dated counts as
    progress-less rather than as old: an undatable round is never closed."""
    expected, received, progress = set(), set(), ""
    for r in rows:
        if int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) != iter_:
            continue
        role = r.get("role")
        if role not in ("assistant", "tool"):
            continue
        rec = str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")
        if rec > progress:
            progress = rec
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if role == "assistant":
            items = t if isinstance(t, list) else [t]
            expected.update(x.get("id", "") for x in items
                            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "tool_call"
                            and x.get("id"))
        else:
            items = t if isinstance(t, list) else ([] if t is None else [t])
            received.update(x.get("id") for x in items
                            if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("id"))
    return expected, received, progress


def rebuild(rows):
    """The cumulative thread, in provider order: for each iteration the user
    turn, then the assistant bundle, then its results."""
    out = []
    def order(r):
        # A `receipt` sorts LAST, ahead of no round: it arrives on a foreign
        # chain that carries no context, so the ear can only file it under
        # iteration 0 -- and a refusal buried between two tool rounds refuses
        # something the thread has not shown yet.
        late = 1 if r.get("role") == "receipt" else 0
        return (late, 0 if late else int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0),
                {"user": 0, "assistant": 1}.get(r.get("role"), 2),
                str(r.get("recorded_at") or ""))

    for r in sorted(rows, key=order):
        # A `caller` row is a NOTE the loop keeps about itself, a `system` row
        # is the prompt the build was briefed with (GH #477), and an `interim`
        # row is half of a provider message whose other half is already in the
        # thread (GH #485). None of the three is a turn, and handing one to a
        # provider would be a message nobody wrote -- or, for `interim`, the
        # same message twice, split across the results it was supposed to
        # precede.
        if r.get("role") in ("caller", "system", "interim"):
            continue
        try:
            t = json.loads(r.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if isinstance(t, list):
            out.extend(x for x in t if isinstance(x, dict))
        elif isinstance(t, dict):
            out.append(t)
    return out


def writing_round(nxt):
    """Whether round `nxt` is one of the rounds reserved for writing."""
    return nxt + WRITE_ROUNDS > MAX_ITER


def budget(nxt):
    """What round `nxt` may spend, in the words the composer reads.

    Recomputed here rather than parked with the prompt: `brief` runs once per
    build and the number changes every round, so a budget written into the
    parked instructions would be round 0's budget forever. This cell already
    holds both numbers -- it stamps them on every emission that closes a round
    -- and until GH #485 it kept them to itself."""
    total, human = MAX_ITER + 1, nxt + 1
    if writing_round(nxt):
        return ("BUDGET -- this is round %d of %d, and it is a WRITING round: "
                "no tools are offered in it, because the looking is over. "
                "Answer with the manifest, {\"declarations\": [...]}, or -- if "
                "an OPERATOR's fact you were never given is missing -- with "
                "{\"question\": \"...\"}. Anything else ends the build as "
                "design_budget_exhausted: paid for, and nothing delivered."
                % (human, total))
    return ("BUDGET -- this is round %d of %d. %d further round(s) may call "
            "tools; after them comes the WRITING round, which is offered no "
            "tools at all. Spend what is left on what you cannot answer "
            "without, and remember that a call answering the way an earlier "
            "one did is the corpus saying it has nothing more. A draft the "
            "door refuses by name comes back to you and is repairable; an "
            "empty answer comes back as nothing."
            % (human, total, max(0, MAX_ITER - WRITE_ROUNDS - nxt)))


def briefed(out, rows, nxt):
    """GH #477 -- the INSTRUCTIONS ride back out on every round that re-enters
    the composer.

    `brief` publishes the grammar, the endpoint rule, the tool schemas and the
    scope line exactly once, and it is never asked again: round 1 onwards is
    briefed by this loop. A thread rebuilt from the rows alone therefore reached
    an `llm` cell with no system tree at all -- and a model that can no longer
    see the grammar writes a draft the door refuses, or asks what it was
    supposed to build. The tree is parked beside the question (role `system`)
    and handed back here VERBATIM: one spelling of the prompt, never two."""
    named = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "system"]
    if not named:
        return out
    newest = max(named, key=lambda r: str(r.get("recorded_at") or ""))
    try:
        tree = json.loads(newest.get("turn") or "null")
    except Exception:
        return out
    if isinstance(tree, dict) and tree:
        tree = dict(tree)
        # The one slot that is NOT parked: it is different every round, so it is
        # rendered here. It has no entry in `compose`'s `system_order`, which
        # puts it after the ordered slots -- last in the prompt, which is where
        # a rule about THIS round belongs.
        tree["budget"] = {"text": budget(nxt)}
        # `$replace` at the ROOT (GH #264): the prompt of this round is exactly
        # what this message carries. An `llm` cell UPSERTS the system tree it is
        # sent into its own cell.db per slot path, and this composer is ONE cell
        # for every build in the colony -- so a slot that is merely left out of a
        # message is not gone, it is remembered. Measured: the writing round
        # below dropped `tools` from the body and the model still answered
        # `finish_reason: tool_calls`, because the menu of the round before it
        # was still in the store (S13, first walk). It is also GH #477's "one
        # spelling of the prompt" made true against residue: two builds in one
        # colony cannot leak a prompt into each other.
        tree["$replace"] = True
        if writing_round(nxt):
            # The menu is WITHHELD, not forbidden in prose. `concat_system_prompt`
            # skips `system.tools` and `build_openai_request` reads it for the
            # request's `tools` array, so with the slot revoked there is no array
            # and a tool call is not a move the wire admits.
            tree.pop("tools", None)
        out["system"] = tree
    return out


def caller_row():
    """The caller, parked beside the round it belongs to."""
    said = dict(caller)
    said["orig_request"] = str(ctx.get("orig_request") or "")
    return ("w-caller-row",
            {"operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
             "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": it, "role": "caller",
                     "turn": json.dumps(said), "fired": 0,
                     "recorded_at": now}})


# ---- Lane: the composer asked for tools. The assistant turn IS the expectation
# set, and it is parked before any result can reach us (PLAIN order at the
# dispatcher guarantees it arrives first).
#
# It is also the one leg of a round that is always on the BUILD's own chain, so
# it is where the caller is written down. Only when the context actually names
# SOMETHING: an empty row would shadow a good one on the read-back, and a build
# driven without the tool surface has no caller to lose. Any of the keys is
# enough -- an operator names a door and no call id, an agent names a call id
# and no door, and both have something to lose (GH #480).
if hop.get("route") == "calls":
    before = [caller_row()] if names_a_caller(caller) else []
    emit([park_and_read("assistant", msgs, before=before)])

# ---- Lane: the composer said something BESIDE its bundle (GH #485).
#
# `dispatcher@1.2.0` splits one model answer into two emissions when it carries
# content and tool calls at once: the bundle on `calls`, the sentence on
# `answer` with `hop.interim` set (GH #378). This hive drew no edge for the
# second one, so every round in which a hosted model narrated -- which is most
# of them -- left a `no_route` dead letter beside a round that otherwise worked.
#
# It is written down and never replayed. An interim sentence and its own bundle
# are ONE provider message; re-entering the thread as a second `assistant` turn
# would put it between a bundle and its results, which is a message order no
# OpenAI-shaped endpoint accepts (`rebuild` skips the role for that reason). And
# it parks WITHOUT a read-back: this leg answers no tool_call, so it must not
# join the round election it did not open.
if hop.get("route") == "answer":
    if not build_id:
        park()
    emit([store_bundle([
        ("w-interim-row",
         {"operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
          "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": it, "role": "interim",
                  "turn": json.dumps(msgs[0] if msgs else {}), "fired": 0,
                  "recorded_at": now}})])])

# ---- Lane: one tool answered.
if hop.get("operation") == "tool_result" or hop.get("route") == "unknown":
    turn = msgs[0] if msgs else {}
    emit([park_and_read("tool", turn)])

# ---- Lane: a receipt came back from the submitter (the refine ear).
#
# It arrives on a FOREIGN chain. `templates/submit/gate` renders a receipt off
# its own remembered row -- "the colony's answer begins a fresh trace and
# carries neither" -- and the `./submit -> ./builder` edge re-stamps `hop.route`
# and nothing else. So `context.repairs` is 0 or absent here no matter what the
# loop counted, and the budget is NOT decided on this lane. It is decided on the
# read-back below, from the rows, which is the only counter that survives.
if hop.get("route") == "in_receipt":
    code = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
    said = ""
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("text"):
            said = str(m["text"])
    if repairs >= MAX_REPAIRS:
        # A belt, not the truth: when the context DID survive and already says
        # the budget is spent, there is no reason to write another row first.
        # Named, never silent, and never an empty manifest.
        emit([{"header": head("give_up", {"error_code": code or "repair_budget_spent"}),
               "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                             "text": "the build stops after %d repair(s): %s -- %s"
                                     % (repairs, code, said[:600])}]}])
    # NAME the code in the turn. The model only sees the turn, and a refusal it
    # cannot name is one it cannot repair.
    #
    # Role `receipt`, not `tool`: a refusal answers no tool_call, so `round_sets`
    # -- which reads `assistant` and `tool` only -- must not count it as an
    # answer, while `rebuild` still carries it to the composer. It is also what
    # the read-back below counts the budget from.
    text = REFUSED + (code or "unnamed")
    if said:
        text += " -- " + said[:600]

    # NOT a `tool_result` turn. This thread goes straight back into
    # `compose`, an llm cell: an id-less tool_result renders as
    # {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": ""}, a message that answers no call,
    # and the provider refuses the WHOLE request with 400 (measured 3 of 3,
    # in the 2026-08-27 builder agentic-loop run series).
    # A refusal answers no tool_call because it comes from the refine lane,
    # so it travels as the plain turn docs/cell-types.md sanctions for a
    # result used outside a tool loop -- carrying no id at all.
    turn = {"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": text}
    if build_id:
        emit([park_and_read("receipt", turn)])
    # No build_id -- the REAL wire, and the reason this cell correlates by
    # digest at all. The submitter parks and pops a submission under
    # `manifest_sha256`, so that is the one handle that survives the round trip;
    # `normalise` wrote down which build the digest belongs to. Stage the
    # refusal UNDER the digest so two builds refused at the same moment cannot
    # pool into one, and ask who owns it in the same bundle.
    sha = str(hop.get("manifest_sha256") or "")
    if not sha:
        emit([{"header": head("give_up", {"error_code": "build_unknown"}),
               "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                             "text": "a refusal arrived with neither a build nor "
                                     "a manifest digest -- %s" % text}]}])
    emit([store_bundle([
        ("w-receipt-row",
         {"operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
          "row": {"build_id": sha, "iter": it, "role": "receipt",
                  "turn": json.dumps(turn), "fired": 0, "recorded_at": now}}),
        ("w-build-lookup",
         {"operation": "select", "table": "thread",
          "columns": ["build_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired", "recorded_at"],
          "where": {"role": "manifest", "turn": sha}})])])

# ---- Lane: the store answered. This is where the round is decided.
if hop.get("route") == "cstore" or hop.get("operation") in ("bundle", "select"):
    # ---- The binding lookup answered: who owns this manifest digest?
    if has_slot(d, "w-build-lookup"):
        binds = rows_of(d, "w-build-lookup")
        newest = max(binds, key=lambda r: str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")) if binds else {}
        owner = str(newest.get("build_id") or "")
        if not owner:
            # A digest nobody in this hive composed. It must NOT park: a
            # refusal that cannot find its build is still a build that stopped.
            emit([{"header": head("give_up", {"error_code": "build_unknown"}),
                   "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                                 "text": "no build in this hive composed the "
                                         "refused manifest"}]}])
        # Two builds that drafted byte-identical manifests share a digest; the
        # NEWEST binding wins, and either of them is repairing the same bytes.
        emit([store_bundle([
            ("w-adopt",
             {"operation": "update", "table": "thread",
              "set": {"build_id": owner},
              "where": {"build_id": str(newest.get("turn") or ""),
                        "role": "receipt"}}),
            ("w-round-read",
             {"operation": "select", "table": "thread",
              "columns": ["build_id", "iter", "role", "turn", "fired", "recorded_at"],
              "where": {"build_id": owner}})])])

    rows = rows_of(d, "w-round-read")
    if not rows:
        park()
    # The slate says whose it is. On the receipt road the context arrived empty
    # and the adopt bundle above put the rows under their build, so this is
    # where the cell learns the name it will claim with.
    if not build_id:
        build_id = str(rows[0].get("build_id") or "")
        # GH #501 -- and the ROUND counter comes off the slate for exactly the
        # reason the repair counter does. The context arrived EMPTY (a receipt
        # travels on the submitter's chain), so `it` is 0 here whatever the loop
        # counted -- and a repair stamped with 0 re-enters a loop whose only cap
        # is `int(context.iter) < MAX_ITER`, which hands a refused build a second
        # full round budget on a wish whose briefing named one. Every row of a
        # build carries the round it belongs to, so the highest of them IS the
        # round the build reached. Read only in here: on the loop's own chain the
        # context is the counter and it is the one that is right -- the slate can
        # hold rows of a round that has not been decided yet.
        it = max([int(r.get("iter") or 0) for r in rows] + [it])
    # The caller, read back off the slate -- the half GH #460 is about, and the
    # door GH #480 is about. On a round an eye won, the context arrived with the
    # three loop coordinates and nothing else; on a receipt it arrived empty.
    # The row parked when the composer opened the round is where the requester
    # and its door survived. Newest wins, and a row naming NOTHING is never
    # allowed to shadow one that does.
    parked_callers = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "caller"]
    said = None
    if parked_callers:
        newest_caller = max(parked_callers,
                            key=lambda r: str(r.get("recorded_at") or ""))
        try:
            said = json.loads(newest_caller.get("turn") or "null")
        except Exception:
            said = None
    if not isinstance(said, dict):
        said = None
    if said and not names_a_caller(caller):
        for k in CALLER_KEYS:
            caller[k] = str(said.get(k) or "")
    # WHICH LANE composed this build, off the same row (GH #480, second half).
    # The fast lane parks a caller row of its own -- `templates/builder/recipes`,
    # filed under the digest, because a model-free build has no other identity --
    # and marks it, and the mark is read here and nowhere else.
    lane = str((said or {}).get("build_lane") or "")
    # ---- The refine ear's read-back, and it is decided BEFORE the fired check:
    # a receipt refuses a round that has fired by definition, so the guard that
    # keeps a late tool result out would silently swallow every repair -- and a
    # build that stops has to say so.
    #
    # The budget is COUNTED FROM THE ROWS, never carried. A receipt arrives on a
    # foreign chain that drops every counter the loop set (see the in_receipt
    # lane), so `context.repairs` is worthless here -- but the refusals are all
    # written down, and counting them is exact. `fired` is the hand-back claim,
    # the same column and the same discipline the round election uses: an open
    # receipt is one the composer has not seen, and claiming it is what stops a
    # later read-back of the same slate from handing it back twice.
    receipts = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "receipt"]
    open_receipts = [r for r in receipts if not int(r.get("fired") or 0)]
    if open_receipts:
        done = len(receipts)
        newest = max(open_receipts,
                     key=lambda r: str(r.get("recorded_at") or ""))
        code = code_of(newest)
        # One claim for both exits: a give_up that left its receipt open would
        # be emitted again by the next read-back of the same slate.
        claim = {"header": head("cstore", {"repairs": str(done)}),
                 "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                               "id": "w-repair-done",
                               "text": json.dumps({
                                   "operation": "update", "table": "thread",
                                   "set": {"fired": 1},
                                   "where": {"build_id": build_id,
                                             "role": "receipt", "fired": 0}})}]}
        # GH #480 -- the short road, and it is a decision rather than a shortcut.
        # A recipe is a pure function of the wish: no composer opened a round,
        # there is no thread to hand back and no question to re-ask, so a repair
        # round would call a model that never ran to re-derive bytes that were
        # already determined. What a model-free refusal needs is its NAME and the
        # door it came from -- and the caller row above is where that door
        # survived the submitter's chain.
        if lane == "recipe":
            emit([{"header": head("give_up", {"repairs": str(done),
                                              "error_code": code or "unnamed"}),
                   "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                                 "text": "the model-free build stops: %s -- a "
                                         "recipe has no composer to repair with"
                                         % (code or "unnamed")}]},
                  claim])
        if done > MAX_REPAIRS:
            emit([{"header": head("give_up", {"repairs": str(done),
                                              "error_code": code or "repair_budget_spent"}),
                   "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                                 "text": "the build stops after %d repair(s): %s"
                                         % (MAX_REPAIRS, code or "unnamed")}]},
                  claim])
        # A repair re-enters the round it is repairing, not a new one: the
        # counter arrives EMPTY on the receipt lane (foreign chain), so `it` is
        # whatever survived, and the budget is stated for that round.
        emit([briefed({"header": head("repair", {"repairs": str(done)}),
                       "messages": rebuild(rows)}, rows, it), claim])
    # The mark makes the election permanent: a result arriving after its round
    # answered reads a complete set too, and without this it would send the
    # thread to the composer a second time.
    if any(int(r.get("fired") or 0) for r in rows
           if r.get("role") == "assistant" and int(r.get("iter", 0) or 0) == it):
        park()
    expected, received, progress = round_sets(rows, it)
    missing = expected - received
    if expected and missing and progress and progress < IDLE_CUT:
        # The deterministic exit: the round went idle with calls open and a
        # message reached us anyway. Stand-ins complete the fan-in and
        # everything after this is the regular machine.
        emit([park_and_read("tool",
                            {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": mid,
                             "text": "tool result lost: the round went idle "
                                     "before this call's result arrived"})
              for mid in sorted(missing)])
    if not expected or missing:
        park()

    spent = it >= MAX_ITER
    claim = {"header": head("cstore"),
             "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call",
                           "id": "w-round-done",
                           "text": json.dumps({
                               "operation": "update", "table": "thread",
                               "set": {"fired": 1},
                               "where": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": it,
                                         "role": "assistant", "fired": 0}})}]}
    thread = rebuild(rows)
    # `iter` is a COORDINATE -- the round this emission closed, counted from
    # zero -- and it stays one: the slate is keyed on it, the repair edge
    # restores context.iter from it, and a scenario asserts it. What an
    # onlooker wants is a COUNT, and reading the coordinate as one made an
    # acceptance run report 0 of 4 for a loop that had looked 4 of 4
    # (builder-agentic-loop-messlauf.md, acceptance table, line 4). So the count is stamped
    # beside it, on the two routes that actually close a round.
    extra = {"round_capped": "1" if spent else "0",
             "rounds_done": str(it + 1),
             # The count an ONLOOKER wants, forwards. `rounds_done` says what
             # was spent; a reader deciding whether a build is worth waiting for
             # needs what is left, and reading the one as the other is the
             # mistake `rounds_done` was added against (GH #485).
             "rounds_left": str(max(0, MAX_ITER - (it + 1))),
             "round_stale": "1" if any("tool result lost" in str(x.get("text", ""))
                                       for x in thread) else "0"}
    out = {"header": head("draft" if spent else "fire", extra),
           "messages": thread}
    # Only the route that re-enters the COMPOSER is re-briefed: `draft` leaves
    # for `normalise`, which reads a manifest out of the last turn and has no
    # use for a prompt.
    if not spent:
        out = briefed(out, rows, it + 1)
    emit([out, claim])

park()

max_iter.description: BUILDER_MAX_ITER -- how many tool rounds one build may take. The loop begins at this seam, so this seam ends it: at the cap the collected thread leaves for `normalise` with hop.round_capped=1 instead of asking the composer again. It is NOT the dispatcher's call budget, which bounds one answer's bundle and lives at the dispatcher because only that cell sees the whole bundle.

write_rounds.description: BUILDER_WRITE_ROUNDS -- how many of a build's LAST rounds are writing rounds: rounds the composer is asked with no tool menu at all, so a tool call is not a move the wire admits and the manifest is the only answer left. A THIRD budget beside max_iter and max_repairs, and separate for the same reason they are: a model that spends every round it has on looking has none left for the answer, and looking is what a model does when nothing stops it (GH #485 -- seven rounds, thirteen tool calls, not one text turn). It costs the last round of the round budget, not an extra one.

max_repairs.description: BUILDER_MAX_REPAIRS -- how often a refused draft may be handed back to the composer with its error_code named. Deliberately a SEPARATE budget from max_iter: a model that spent its round budget on searches would have none left for the refusal it could actually repair. At the cap the build stops on the error lane with the code that refused it, never with an empty manifest.

round_idle_ms.description: BUILDER_ROUND_IDLE_MS -- idle window of one tool round. A round whose last progress lies behind this window while its fan-in is incomplete is closed at the NEXT message that reaches this cell anyway: the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results keeping their tool_call_id, then the round fires through its regular route with hop.round_stale=1. It matters because a /colony eye CAN stay silent -- it has no cell.db and no timer, so it cannot notice its own silence -- and a TTL death emits nothing at all towards the surface.

description.purpose: The fan-in of the builder's tool loop, and the only place the loop can end. It parks every turn of a build in the `thread` table and reads the slate back in the SAME message (GH #419), so of N tool legs parking concurrently exactly one reads a complete round -- membership of call ids, never a row count, so arrival order cannot change the answer and a duplicate id cannot fake a set. The winning leg rebuilds the cumulative thread -- the question `brief` parked at the head of the build included, and with the instruction tree it parked beside it handed back in the body's `system` slot, because this cell is what briefs every round after the first (GH #477) -- sends it back over the re-entry edge on route `fire`, and claims the round in the same multi-send by setting `fired=1` on the assistant row: a result that arrives after its round was answered reads a complete set too, and the mark is what makes the election permanent. A refusal from the submitter takes the same road in the other direction: it is parked as a `receipt` row with its error_code NAMED in the turn (a refusal the model cannot name is one it cannot repair), and the read-back hands the thread back to the composer on route `repair` as long as the slate holds more receipts than context.repairs counts hand-backs -- the comparison is the whole guard, monotone and readable from the slate. Three bounds are its own, because `restore_ttl` on the re-entry edge deliberately takes TTL out of the game: params.max_iter ends the loop here (the thread leaves for `normalise` with hop.round_capped=1 instead of asking the composer again), params.max_repairs ends a refusal loop on route `give_up` with the error_code that refused it, and params.round_idle_ms closes a round whose result never came -- the missing calls get synthetic error tool_results keeping their tool_call_id, and the round fires through the REGULAR machine with hop.round_stale=1.
description.use_when: Beside `transcript`, inside the builder hive: on the dispatcher's assistant turn (route `calls`), on every tool result of the eyes and of the librarian, on an `unknown` refusal, on the store's own bundle reply, and on the refine ear `in_receipt`. The re-entry edge `./weave -> ./compose` carries the counters AND `restore_ttl`.
description.not_in_scope: No inference, no rendering, no manifest of its own -- what leaves on `draft` is the collected thread and `normalise` decides what a manifest is. No fan-OUT: naming the cell behind a tool is an edge's decision at `dispatcher`. No timer and no schedule of its own: the idle exit is pure arithmetic over `recorded_at`, evaluated at the next message that reaches this cell anyway. No deletion and no retention: a build is minutes long. No second reader of the round table -- a second reader would be a second protocol over the same guard.
description.emits_meaning: route cstore: store traffic of this cell -- the park-and-read bundle (`w-round-row` + `w-round-read`) and the guarded `fired=1` claim (`w-round-done`), which travels WITH the fire rather than one hop in front of it. route fire: THE re-entry, messages[] the cumulative thread in provider order (the question first, then per iteration the assistant bundle and its results) and body.system the instruction tree `brief` parked -- both routes that re-enter the composer carry it, `fire` and `repair`, and `draft` carries neither because it leaves for `normalise`, which reads a manifest out of the last turn and has no use for a prompt --, hop.iter the COORDINATE of the round it closed -- counted from zero, because the re-entry edge is what raises it -- and hop.rounds_done the COUNT of rounds this build has closed, this one included. The two differ by one and the second exists because the first was read as a count once and reported a loop that had looked as one that never did. hop.round_stale=1 when a synthetic stand-in travels in it. route repair: the SAME thread with a refusal at the end of it, on its way back to the composer -- emitted when the slate holds more `receipt` rows than context.repairs counts hand-backs, which is what makes the re-entry edge raise the counter and what makes the repair budget reachable at all. route draft: the thread when the iteration budget is spent, with hop.round_capped=1 and hop.rounds_done -- the loop ends where it began. rounds_done rides on fire and draft and nowhere else: a `repair` hands a refusal back without a round having run, and `give_up` and `cstore` close none. route give_up: the repair budget is spent, hop.error_code the code that refused the submission, and never an empty manifest. An incomplete fan-in and a lost race emit NOTHING (empty multi-send, terminal by design). EVERY emission carries the caller beside the loop's own coordinates -- build_call_id, agent, build_op, build_scope and, since GH #480, the DOOR the shell decided on: build_caller and build_auto_submit, present and empty rather than absent -- and every edge out of this cell lifts them back into the context. They come from the context when the round arrived on the build's own chain, and off the `caller` row otherwise: a `/colony` eye's reply starts a fresh trace, so a round an eye WON used to hand the requester a draft under an empty tool_call_id (GH #460) and an operator-initiated build its manifest to an organisation instead of to the front door (GH #480). The row is parked whenever the context names ANY of the six, not only a tool_call_id: an operator has a door and no call id, and used to write nothing down at all.
description.consumes_meaning: Lanes are read from hop: route `calls` (the assistant tool_call turn from the dispatcher -- it IS the expectation set and is parked before any result can reach this cell), hop.operation `tool_result` or route `unknown` (one tool answer, filed under the call it answers), route `in_receipt` (a submitter's refusal, correlated by context.build_id and NAMED in the turn, because a refusal the model cannot name is one it cannot repair), route `cstore` / hop.operation `bundle` (the store's reply, where the round is decided). context carries build_id, iter and repairs; the store's own reply lane carries them back through context.store_origin. context also carries the CALLER -- build_call_id, agent, build_op, build_scope, the door keys build_caller and build_auto_submit, and the prose orig_request -- and route `calls` is where it is written down: that leg is always on the build's own chain, so the row it parks (role `caller`, one JSON object) is what a later round reads back when an eye won the race or when a refusal arrived on the submitter's chain. orig_request stays in the row and never on the hop: a header is not where prose belongs, and the one cell that reads it re-sets it from its own hop on every lookup.
examples: two calls in one bundle -> the assistant row is parked first, then two tool legs park concurrently -> the second one reads assistant+2 results, fires the thread on `fire` and claims the row in the same message; the first one read an incomplete set and emitted nothing
a third, late result for the same round -> it reads a complete set as well, sees fired=1 on the assistant row and parks: the mark makes the election permanent

a /colony eye stays silent -> the round parks; the next message that reaches this cell after params.round_idle_ms writes a 'tool result lost' stand-in under the missing tool_call_id, the fan-in completes through the regular machine and the thread fires with hop.round_stale=1
the model asks for tools a seventh time with params.max_iter=6 -> at iter == max_iter the thread leaves on `draft` with hop.round_capped=1 instead of re-entering the composer

the submitter refuses with requirement_missing and context.repairs=0 -> the code is parked as a `receipt` row naming it, the read-back finds one arrival against zero hand-backs and sends the whole thread back to the composer on `repair`; the re-entry edge raises context.repairs, so the same slate read again hands nothing back

the same refusal at repairs == params.max_repairs -> nothing is parked at all and the build leaves on `give_up` with hop.error_code=requirement_missing: a build that stops says so, it never falls silent

two eyes and one librarian answer the same round and the second EYE arrives last -> the context it carries names build_id, iter and repairs and nothing else, so the fan-in reads the `caller` row off the slate and fires the thread with the requester's tool_call_id on it; without the row the draft would come back under an empty id and the tool round that asked would never close, and an operator-initiated build gets its front door back the same way -- without it the manifest is delivered into an organisation, which in a fresh colony is empty by construction and therefore a silent dead letter (GH #480)
